info.name: ATW Backend - Admin API
info.description:
# ATW Backend — Admin API

Admin authentication, account self-service, permission catalog, and staff/role administration for the Anytime Work backend. This is the **admin side only** — ATW's own internal platform staff/employees (e.g. `AdminStaffController`, roles like "Senior Developer"). Worker-side and company-side auth are separate, not-yet-built modules and are out of scope for this collection.

Every endpoint is versioned under `/api/v1/` and returns the same envelope:

```
{ "success": boolean, "data": <payload> | null, "error": <ApiError> | null }
```

`ApiError` shape: `{"code": string, "message": string, "fieldErrors": [{"field","message"}] | null, "timestamp": ISO-8601 string, "traceId": string | null}`. `fieldErrors` is populated only for `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses that came from `@Valid` request-body validation; it's `null`/omitted for every other error, including other `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses raised programmatically (e.g. "Unknown permission code(s)"). `traceId` echoes the `X-Correlation-Id` request header when present — include it when reporting a bug.

## Running this collection

Select the **ATW Backend - Local** environment first. Requests are grouped Auth → Account → Admin → Roles → Staff → Health, roughly the order you'd run them in:

1. **Auth > Login**, then **Auth > Verify OTP** (skip if `otpRequired` was `false`) — saves `{{accessToken}}` / `{{refreshToken}}`.
2. Locally, `atw.admin.security.otp-in-response=true` (see `application-local.properties`) puts the plaintext code straight into the response as `testOtp`; this collection's Tests scripts save it to `{{testOtp}}`, which Verify OTP's body already references — so steps 1-2 work with zero manual copy-pasting on a local run. This flag is hard-refused at startup outside local/test (`StartupSecurityValidator`); anywhere else, read the OTP from the real email or server log (`MAIL_PROVIDER=log`) and paste it in by hand.
3. **Roles > Create Role** and **Staff > Create Staff** save `{{roleId}}` / `{{staffId}}` for the requests below them.
4. `{{resetToken}}` (Forgot/Reset Password) and `{{inviteToken}}` (Create Staff → Accept Invite) are **not** auto-populated — they only ever reach an inbox or the server log, by design, so copy them in manually from there.

## Error codes that can appear on (almost) any endpoint

These are produced centrally — by `GlobalExceptionHandler`, by Spring Security's entry point / access-denied handler, or by the two security filters that run before a controller is even reached — so they are **not** re-documented on every individual request below; only an endpoint's *specific* codes and triggers are. Two pairs are easy to confuse and worth reading carefully:

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | A `@Valid` request-body field failed Bean Validation (`fieldErrors[]` present), or a service-level input check failed (no `fieldErrors`). |
| `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | 400 | Request body is missing or isn't valid JSON. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | `Content-Type` isn't `application/json`. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | **No bearer token was presented at all**, or it's malformed/expired/signature-invalid. Produced by Spring Security itself, before any controller runs. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | A **business-level** auth failure on an endpoint that doesn't require a token in the first place — bad login credentials, a locked/disabled account, an invalid refresh/reset/invite token. Same HTTP status as `UNAUTHENTICATED` above, different meaning: this means "the token/credential you supplied is bad", not "you supplied nothing". |
| `SESSION_REVOKED` | 401 | The bearer token parses fine, but the admin's `security_version` has moved on since it was issued (password changed/reset, or their role assignment changed), or the account is no longer `ACTIVE`. The client must discard tokens and log in again — refreshing won't help, the refresh token was revoked too. |
| `MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD` | 403 | Authenticated, but the token's `mustChangePassword` flag is set and this isn't `/admin/account/me` or `/admin/account/change-password`. |
| `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 | Authenticated, but lacking the specific permission the endpoint requires. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests to one of the 6 public, abuse-prone auth endpoints from the same IP within the window — default 10 requests/60s, **per endpoint**, not pooled across them. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The **URL itself** doesn't match any endpoint (a routing miss — typo'd path, wrong version prefix, etc). |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The URL is valid, but the specific id in it (a staff id, role id, ...) doesn't exist. Different from `NOT_FOUND` above — don't conflate "no such route" with "no such record". |
| `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | 405 | Right URL, wrong HTTP verb. |
| `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | Input is syntactically well-formed but violates a business rule (e.g. "system roles cannot be modified", a privilege-escalation attempt, self/super-admin protection). |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | Either an endpoint's own duplicate check (most common — a friendlier, specific message), or a generic last-resort safety net when a unique-constraint violation reaches the database despite an earlier application-level check passing (a genuine race between two concurrent requests) — that fallback case always carries the same generic message, regardless of which field collided. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Full detail (stack trace) is logged server-side against the same `traceId` returned to the client; never returned in the response body itself. |

## Documentation cross-references

- `docs/admin-auth-api.md` — narrative walkthrough of the auth flow.
- `FRONTEND_HANDOVER.md` / `HANDOVER.md` — broader project handover context, including what's explicitly **out of scope** today (worker/company auth, an audit-log read API, session/device listing, a resend-invite endpoint).

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Public endpoints under `/api/v1/admin/auth/**` — **no bearer token required, and none should be sent** (these paths are explicitly listed in `SecurityConfig.PUBLIC_PATHS` and are also exempted from the must-change-password gate in `AdminSessionPolicyFilter`).

All of these except **Refresh** and **Logout** are rate-limited at 10 requests/60s per IP, per endpoint (see the collection-level error table for `RATE_LIMITED`) — Refresh is excluded because it's routine traffic, not abuse-prone; Logout is excluded because there's nothing to abuse (it always succeeds).

Run order for a full login: **Login → Verify OTP** (skip Verify OTP if `otpRequired` came back `false`). **Resend OTP** is an alternative branch off Login, not part of the main sequence.

request.description:
**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited:** yes, own 10 req/60s-per-IP bucket.

Step 1 of login: verifies the password only. `usernameOrEmail` is matched case-insensitively against either the username or the email (`findByUsernameIgnoreCaseOrEmailIgnoreCase`).

**Validation**
- `usernameOrEmail` — required, non-blank.
- `password` — required, non-blank.

**Behavior / errors** (checked in this order; the first match wins)

| Condition | Code | HTTP | Audit action |
|---|---|---|---|
| No admin matches the identifier | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | `LOGIN_FAILED` |
| Account is currently locked (see below) | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | `LOGIN_BLOCKED` |
| Account `status = DISABLED` | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | `LOGIN_BLOCKED` |
| Password doesn't match | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | `LOGIN_FAILED` |

Note: the locked/disabled messages ("Account is temporarily locked...", "Account is disabled.") are intentionally more specific than the generic "Invalid credentials" used for the other two rows — a caller who knows a valid identifier can distinguish "wrong password" from "this account is locked/disabled". This is a deliberate, pre-existing trade-off (better operational feedback vs. a small account-existence signal), not an oversight — contrast with Forgot Password below, which *is* designed to reveal nothing.

**Lockout policy:** 5 wrong passwords in a row (default `ADMIN_MAX_FAILED_LOGINS`) locks the account for 15 minutes (default `ADMIN_LOCKOUT_DURATION`). Any successful password check resets the counter to 0, including one that's followed by this account later failing OTP — the counter is purely about the password step.

**On success:**
- If `atw.admin.security.otp-enabled` (default **true**): issues an OTP (see Verify OTP), emails it (template `ADMIN_LOGIN_OTP`), audits `LOGIN_OTP_SENT`, and responds `{otpRequired: true, challengeId, testOtp}` — call **Verify OTP** next.
- If OTP is disabled: logs the admin in immediately, audits `LOGIN_SUCCESS`, and responds `{otpRequired: false, tokens: {...}}` where `tokens` has the exact same shape as Verify OTP's response body (`AuthTokens`).

`testOtp` is only ever present when `atw.admin.security.otp-in-response=true` — true in `application-local.properties`, hard-refused at startup in any non-local/test profile (`StartupSecurityValidator`). This collection's Tests script saves it to `{{testOtp}}`, which the Verify OTP request body already references.

exec: console.log('OTP required - challengeId (and testOtp, if present) saved. Run Verify OTP next.');

request.description:
**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited:** yes, own 10 req/60s-per-IP bucket.

Step 2: submits the code for the `challengeId` from Login/Resend OTP.

**Validation**
- `challengeId` — required, must be a UUID.
- `otp` — required, non-blank (compared as a string; leading zeros matter).

**Behavior / errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `challengeId` doesn't exist, OR the challenge is already consumed, OR it's past `otpTtl` (default 10 min) | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| The challenge already has `otpMaxAttempts` (default 5) recorded wrong guesses | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "Too many invalid attempts. Please request a new code." |
| Wrong code | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 — and the attempt counter above is incremented, **even on this failing response** (it's persisted before the exception is thrown) |
| Code is correct, but the admin's account was disabled between Login step 1 and now | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 — "Account is disabled." |

Once `otpMaxAttempts` is hit, that challenge is permanently dead — submitting the *correct* code no longer works either. Get a new one via **Resend OTP**, or start over at **Login**.

**On success:** consumes the challenge, clears the account's failed-login counter, records `lastLoginAt`, audits `LOGIN_SUCCESS`, and returns the full `AuthTokens` payload directly (not wrapped in another object, unlike Login's response) — `{accessToken, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn, refreshToken, admin: {...}}`. Check `admin.mustChangePassword`: if true, the frontend should route straight to a change-password screen, since every endpoint except `/account/me` and `/account/change-password` will reject with `MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD` until it's cleared.

**Concurrency:** safe under truly concurrent verify attempts against the same challenge (e.g. a double-submit) — each concurrent guess is still recorded as its own attempt via optimistic-lock retry, so the attempt counter can't be bypassed by racing requests.

response.name: 200 - Authenticated
422 - Too many invalid attempts

request.description:
**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited:** yes, own 10 req/60s-per-IP bucket (independent of the resend-specific cap below).

Issues a fresh code for the same login attempt and **immediately invalidates** the previous challenge — the old `challengeId` stops working for Verify OTP the moment this succeeds, whether or not it had any attempts left.

**Validation**
- `challengeId` — required, must be a UUID.

**Behavior / errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challengeId` doesn't exist at all | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid verification request" |
| It exists but is already consumed or expired | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired verification code" |
| Less than `otpResendInterval` (default 60s) has passed since the previous code was issued | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | "Please wait before requesting another code." |
| This chain has already been resent `otpMaxResends` (default 3) times | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | "Too many resend attempts. Please start over by logging in again." |
| A concurrent resend/verify of the same challenge wins the race | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired verification code" (fails cleanly, not a 500) |

**On success:** returns `{challengeId, testOtp}` with a **new** challenge id and a fresh `otpTtl`. The resend count carries over onto the new challenge (so the cap tracks the whole chain, not just one challenge), audits `LOGIN_OTP_RESENT`, and re-sends the OTP email. This request's Tests script overwrites `{{challengeId}}` (and `{{testOtp}}`, if present) with the new values.

**Permission:** none (public, but requires a valid refresh token). **Rate limited: no** — deliberately excluded from the 6 rate-limited endpoints (`AdminAuthPaths.RATE_LIMITED`); refresh is routine traffic (called every time the 15-minute access token expires), not abuse-prone the way login/OTP/password-reset are.

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a brand-new access+refresh pair, **rotating** the refresh token: the old one is revoked and linked to the new one, so it cannot be used again under any circumstance.

**Validation**
- `refreshToken` — required, non-blank (the opaque token string from a prior auth response, not a JWT).

**Behavior / errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token not found, or expired, or already revoked for an ordinary reason (explicit logout, account disabled, password change/reset) | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | "Refresh token has expired or been revoked" |
| Token was revoked specifically **because it was already rotated away**, and is now being presented again (reuse/replay) | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | "This session was revoked for your safety. Please log in again." |
| Token is valid, but the admin's account is now `DISABLED` | `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | "Account is disabled." (this also revokes the token being presented) |

**Reuse detection (RFC 6819 §5.2.2.3):** every refresh token belongs to a rotation "family" starting at login. Replaying an already-rotated token is a strong signal of theft (an attacker and the legitimate user both holding a copy, one of them having already used it to rotate forward) — detecting this **revokes the entire family**, not just the presented token, cutting off whichever side currently holds the live descendant and forcing a fresh login for both. Audited as `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED`.

**On success:** audits `TOKEN_REFRESHED`, returns a fresh `AuthTokens` (same shape as Verify OTP's response). This request's Tests script overwrites both `{{accessToken}}` and `{{refreshToken}}`.

**Concurrency:** safe against a concurrent password reset/change — both paths take the same per-admin row lock before revoking tokens / bumping the security version, so whichever commits first is what the other observes (no window where a reset "loses" to an in-flight refresh).

**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited: no** — not abuse-prone, deliberately excluded.

Revokes the given refresh token.

**Validation**
- `refreshToken` — required, non-blank.

**Behavior:** always returns `200 success` — there is no error path visible to the client. An unknown or already-revoked token is treated identically to a freshly-valid one (idempotent); only audits `LOGOUT` when the token was actually found.

**Known, deliberate limitation:** this does **not** invalidate the access token the caller was using. JWT access tokens are stateless and not tracked server-side, so they simply remain technically valid until they naturally expire (≤ 15 minutes, `JWT_ACCESS_TTL`). The frontend must also discard the access token client-side immediately on logout — don't rely on the server to reject it. (This was an explicit, accepted trade-off, not an oversight — revoking individual access tokens would require a server-side denylist with its own cost/complexity, and the exposure window is bounded to the access-token TTL.)

**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited:** yes, own 10 req/60s-per-IP bucket.

**Validation**
- `email` — required, must be a syntactically valid email address (format only — existence is deliberately not checked, see below).

**Behavior:** **always** returns `200 success`, whether or not the email belongs to an admin — this is a deliberate anti-enumeration design, unlike Login (see its notes above). Do not treat this response as confirmation the email exists, and don't surface a different UI state based on it.

If the email *does* match an admin: generates an opaque token, stores only its SHA-256 hash (type `PASSWORD_RESET`, TTL `atw.admin.security.password-reset-ttl`, default 30 min), emails a reset link (`{frontendBaseUrl}/admin/reset-password?token=...`), and audits `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`.

**Note:** calling this multiple times for the same admin creates multiple simultaneously-valid reset tokens — an earlier unused link is *not* invalidated just by requesting a new one. All of them (plus any pending login OTP) only get invalidated together once one is actually *used* via Reset Password, or the password is changed via Change Password.

**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited:** yes, own 10 req/60s-per-IP bucket.

Sets a new password from the token in a Forgot Password reset link. `{{resetToken}}` isn't auto-populated by this collection (it only ever reaches the admin's inbox, or the server log with `MAIL_PROVIDER=log`) — copy it from the `token=` query param of the emailed/logged link and set it manually.

**Validation**
- `token` — required, non-blank.
- `newPassword` — required, 8-100 characters.

**Behavior / errors** — all four of the following collapse to the *same* generic message, by design (so a client can't use the error to probe whether a given token value was ever issued, merely expired, or already used):

| Condition | Code | HTTP | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token hash not found | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired reset link" |
| Token exists but isn't type `PASSWORD_RESET` (e.g. it's actually an invite token) | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired reset link" |
| Token already used, or past its TTL | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired reset link" |
| `newPassword` outside 8-100 chars | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Bean Validation message, with `fieldErrors` |

**On success:** sets the new password, bumps `security_version` (every access token issued before this moment stops working immediately, regardless of its remaining TTL), **revokes every refresh token** for that admin (logs out all devices), marks this reset token used, invalidates every *other* outstanding `PASSWORD_RESET` token and every pending login OTP for that admin, emails an "your password was changed" notification, and audits `PASSWORD_RESET`.

**Concurrency:** the admin row is locked before the token is re-checked, specifically to close a race where a sibling reset token (from a second Forgot Password call) is used concurrently — whichever request gets the lock first is the one whose effects "win".

**Permission:** none (public). **Rate limited:** yes, own 10 req/60s-per-IP bucket.

Completes a staff invite issued by **Staff > Create Staff**: sets that brand-new account's *first* real password (it was created with a random, never-disclosed one, so it cannot be used to log in until this runs). `{{inviteToken}}` comes from the `token=` query param of the invite email (or server log, with `MAIL_PROVIDER=log`) — paste it in manually, same as `{{resetToken}}`.

**Validation**
- `token` — required, non-blank.
- `password` — required, 8-100 characters.

**Behavior / errors** — same collapsed-generic-message pattern as Reset Password, for the same reason:

| Condition | Code | HTTP | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token hash not found | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired invite link" |
| Token exists but isn't type `INVITE` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired invite link" |
| Token already used, or past `atw.admin.security.invite-ttl` (default 3 days) | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | "Invalid or expired invite link" |

**On success:** sets the password (which also clears `mustChangePassword` — the new staff member can log in immediately afterward with no forced-change step), bumps `security_version`, marks the invite token used, invalidates every *other* outstanding `INVITE` token for that admin, and audits `STAFF_INVITE_ACCEPTED`.

**Deliberately different from Reset Password:** does **not** revoke refresh tokens (there are none yet — the account has never logged in) and does **not** send a "password changed" email (there's no prior password to notify about). Kept as a fully separate code path precisely so it can skip those steps without touching Reset Password's already-reasoned-through locking behavior, and so the audit trail accurately reflects which event actually happened.

item.name: Account
item.description: Authenticated self-service for the signed-in admin, under `/api/v1/admin/account/**`. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` — no specific permission beyond being authenticated, since every action here targets the caller's own account (there's no `{id}` in any of these paths). `me` and `change-password` are also the only two endpoints reachable while `mustChangePassword` is set.

request.description:
**Permission:** none beyond being authenticated (acts on the caller's own account; reachable even while `mustChangePassword` is set).

Returns the signed-in admin's profile: `{id, username, email, fullName, superAdmin, roles, authorities, mustChangePassword}`. `authorities` is `["SUPER_ADMIN"]` for a super-admin, otherwise the list of effective permission codes from their assigned roles.

The frontend should check `mustChangePassword` right after login/verify-otp and, if true, redirect straight to a change-password screen — every *other* endpoint (this one and Change Password are the only two exceptions) rejects with `MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD` 403 until it's cleared.

**Permission:** none beyond being authenticated.

Returns the effective permission codes for the signed-in admin as a flat array, e.g. `["admin_staff.view", "admin_roles.view", ...]`. A super-admin gets `["*"]` — a wildcard meaning "all permissions", not a literal code to match against the permission catalog. The frontend should special-case `"*"` as all-access rather than trying to look it up.

**Permission:** none beyond being authenticated (reachable even while `mustChangePassword` is set — this is how it gets cleared).

**Validation**
- `currentPassword` — required, non-blank.
- `newPassword` — required, 8-100 characters.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `currentPassword` doesn't match the account's actual password | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 — "Current password is incorrect" |
| `newPassword` outside 8-100 chars | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 — Bean Validation, with `fieldErrors` |

**On success:** sets the new password and clears `mustChangePassword`, bumps `security_version`, **revokes every refresh token** for every device/session, invalidates any outstanding forgot-password reset link and pending login OTP, emails a "password changed" notification, and audits `PASSWORD_CHANGED`.

**Important:** the access token used to make *this* request also stops working immediately afterward (its baked-in security version is now stale) — the frontend must log the user back in, or silently re-authenticate, right after a successful call. Don't assume the current session continues.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Permission-gated endpoints that don't belong to one specific CRUD resource. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the named permission (or super-admin).

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_roles.view`.

Returns the full permission catalog grouped by module — `[{module, permissions: [{code, action, label}]}]`, ordered by module then action — for building a role editor's permission matrix (checkbox grid). There are currently ~23 modules covering every business area (companies, workers, vacancy, payroll, agent, staff, roles, ...); `staff` and `roles` are the two modules relevant to this collection (7 and 4 permission codes respectively).

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Caller lacks `admin_roles.view` | `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 |

item.name: Roles
item.description:
Role CRUD and permission assignment, under `/api/v1/admin/roles/**`. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the matching `admin_roles.*` permission (`admin_roles.view`/`create`/`edit`/`delete` — 4 codes total).

**Privilege-escalation guard** (`PermissionEscalationGuard`, shared with Staff's role-assignment check below): a non-super-admin can never create or edit a role to grant a permission they don't themselves currently hold. This closes a real gap — without it, someone holding `admin_roles.create`/`admin_roles.edit` but not `admin_staff.edit` could still define a role with more power than their own and have it take effect the moment *anyone* assigns it, including editing permissions onto a role that's already assigned to staff. Super-admins are exempt (they implicitly hold every permission).

**System roles** (`systemRole: true`): the 4 seed roles (Sub Admin, and three more including Senior/Junior Developer) are protected from Update and Delete, but can still be *assigned to* or *removed from* staff normally.

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_roles.view`.

Returns every role with its full `permissionCodes` list (no pagination — the role count is small and operator-managed, not user-generated).

response.name: 403 - Missing permission

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_roles.view`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| No role with this id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `admin_roles.create`.

**Validation**
- `name` — required, non-blank, max 100 chars.
- `description` — optional, max 300 chars.
- `permissionCodes` — required list (can be empty `[]` for a role with no permissions yet), each entry non-blank.

**Behavior / errors** (checked in this order)

| Order | Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `name` already used by another role | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| 2 | Any `permissionCodes` entry doesn't exist in the catalog | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 — lists the unknown code(s) by name |
| 3 | Caller is not a super-admin AND `permissionCodes` includes anything they don't themselves currently hold | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "You cannot grant a permission you do not hold yourself." |

Step 2 runs before step 3 deliberately, so a typo'd permission code reports as "unknown code" rather than a confusing "you don't hold this [nonexistent] permission".

**On success:** creates a non-system role (`systemRole: false` — only the 4 seed roles are system roles, and only those are protected from edit/delete), audits `ROLE_CREATED`. This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{roleId}}`.

response.name: 400 - Unknown permission code
422 - Escalation blocked

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_roles.edit`.

Full replace of the role's name, description, and entire permission set (not a merge/patch) — omitted codes are *removed* from the role.

**Validation:** identical to Create Role.

**Behavior / errors** (checked in this order)

| Order | Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Role id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| 2 | Role is a system role (`systemRole: true` — the 4 seed roles) | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "System roles cannot be modified." |
| 3 | `name` already used by a *different* role | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| 4 | Unknown permission code | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| 5 | Escalation (same rule as Create Role) | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

**Important, non-obvious side effect:** every admin currently assigned this role keeps whatever permissions they had **until their access token naturally expires or they make a new authenticated request** — there's no proactive re-login forced here, unlike changing a *staff member's* role assignment (see Update Staff), which does force one. Editing a role's permissions is a slower-moving admin operation; if this surprises you operationally, treat it as something to flag, not rely on silently.

**Permission:** `admin_roles.delete`.

**Behavior / errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Role id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Role is a system role | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "System roles cannot be deleted." |
| One or more staff members are still assigned this role | `CONFLICT` | 409 — "Cannot delete role: N staff member(s) are currently assigned to it. Reassign them first." |

No soft-delete / archive — a successful delete is permanent. There is intentionally no cascade-reassignment; the caller must move affected staff to a different role first (via Update Staff), which is the safer default for an access-control resource.

item.name: Staff
item.description:
Staff/admin account CRUD, role assignment, and the profile/KYC/bank-detail sub-resources, under `/api/v1/admin/staff/**`. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the matching `admin_staff.*` permission (7 codes: `view`/`create`/`edit`/`delete`/`toggle_status`/`view_kyc`/`view_bank_details`).

Same privilege-escalation guard as Roles applies whenever this module assigns roles to a staff member (Create/Update Staff): you cannot hand out a role carrying a permission you don't hold yourself.

**KYC and bank-account-number reads are masked** (all but the last 4 characters replaced with `*`) unless the caller additionally holds `admin_staff.view_kyc` / `admin_staff.view_bank_details` — by default only the **Senior Developer** and **Junior Developer** seed roles hold those two (the same two roles that hold the equivalent sensitive-data permissions for workers, e.g. `workers.view_wallet`). Both values are also **encrypted at rest** (AES-256-GCM) independently of masking — masking controls what a given API caller sees; encryption protects the data if the database itself is ever compromised. The two controls are intentionally layered, not redundant.

Profile/KYC/bank-detail rows are **not** created by Create Staff — they start fully empty (every field `null`) and are populated later via their own PUT endpoints, independently and progressively.

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_staff.view`.

Standard Spring pagination via query params: `page` (0-based), `size`, `sort` (e.g. `sort=fullName,asc`). Returns a `PageResponse<AdminStaffDto>`: `{content: [...], page, size, totalElements, totalPages, first, last}`. KYC/bank fields are **not** included here — fetch them per-staff-member via the sub-resource endpoints below.

response.name: 403 - Missing permission

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_staff.view`.

Returns `AdminStaffDto`: `{id, username, email, fullName, phone, superAdmin, status, roles: [{id, name}], lastLoginAt, createdAt}`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| No staff member with this id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `admin_staff.create`.

**Validation**
- `username` — optional, max 100 chars. An empty string (`""`) is treated identically to `null`/omitted (normalized to `NULL` in storage) — so two staff can both be created with "no username" without colliding on the unique constraint.
- `email` — required, valid email format, max 320 chars.
- `fullName` — required, non-blank, max 150 chars.
- `phone` — optional, max 20 chars.
- `roleIds` — required list (can be `[]`), each a UUID of an existing role.

**No `password` field** — the account is created with a random, cryptographically-generated, never-disclosed password (`mustChangePassword` starts `true`), and an invite email (template `ADMIN_STAFF_INVITE`) is sent with a set-password link — the recipient completes onboarding via **Auth > Accept Invite**. **No `superAdmin` field either** — that flag stays bootstrap-only (seeded at application startup) and is never settable through this API.

**Behavior / errors** (checked in this order)

| Order | Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `email` already belongs to another admin (case-insensitive) | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| 2 | `username` provided and already taken (case-insensitive) | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| 3 | Any `roleIds` entry doesn't exist | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 — "One or more role ids do not exist." |
| 4 | Caller is not a super-admin AND the union of the requested roles' permissions includes anything the caller doesn't themselves hold | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — same escalation guard as Roles |

**On success:** audits `STAFF_CREATED`. This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{staffId}}`. Profile/KYC/bank-detail rows are **not** created here — they start out empty (all-null) and are set separately via the sub-resource endpoints below.

response.name: 200 - Created
409 - Duplicate email

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_staff.edit`.

Full replace of `username`/`fullName`/`phone`/roles. **`email` is intentionally not editable here** — changing a login identifier is treated as a bigger decision than a routine profile edit (not currently exposed through any endpoint).

**Validation:** same as Create Staff, minus `email`.

**Behavior / errors** (checked in this order)

| Order | Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| 2 | Target is a super-admin account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "Super-admin accounts cannot be modified through this endpoint." |
| 3 | `username` provided, changed, and already taken by someone else | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| 4 | Unknown role id | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| 5 | Escalation (same rule as Create Staff) | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

**Side effect — forced re-login, but only when roles actually changed:** if the new role set differs from what the staff member had before, their `security_version` is bumped and every refresh token they hold is revoked, so a permission *removal* takes effect immediately instead of riding out the access token's remaining TTL (up to 15 min). A plain name/phone edit with the same roles does **not** trigger this — don't expect a re-login just from editing `fullName`.

**Permission:** `admin_staff.toggle_status`.

**Validation**
- `status` — required. `status` must be exactly `"ACTIVE"` or `"DISABLED"` — an explicit target, not a toggle, so two quick successive calls can't race into an unintended end state.

**Behavior / errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target is a super-admin account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "Super-admin accounts cannot be deactivated through this endpoint." (message substitutes "activated" when `status: "ACTIVE"`) |
| Target is **your own** account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "You cannot deactivate your own account." (same substitution) |

**Side effect:** setting `DISABLED` immediately revokes every refresh token for that admin (so no new access token can be minted), **and** any access token they're still mid-use with is rejected on its very next request — `AdminSessionPolicyFilter` checks `active` status on every authenticated call, not just at token-issue time. There's no lag waiting for the current token to expire, unlike Logout's known limitation above.

Audits `STAFF_STATUS_CHANGED` with the before→after transition.

response.name: 422 - Cannot disable self

request.description:
**Permission:** `admin_staff.delete`.

**Behavior / errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target is a super-admin account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "Super-admin accounts cannot be deleted through this endpoint." |
| Target is your own account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 — "You cannot delete your own account." |

**Hard delete** — no soft-delete/archive; the row (and its profile/KYC/bank-detail satellite rows, via `ON DELETE CASCADE`) is gone permanently, including its role assignments. Past audit log entries referencing this admin are **not** affected: `admin_audit_log.actor_admin_id` becomes `NULL` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), but `actor_email` is a point-in-time snapshot captured when each log entry was originally written, so "who did this" in historical audit records stays readable even after the actor is deleted.

**Permission:** `admin_staff.view`.

Returns `{dateOfBirth, gender, addressLine, pincode}` — every field is `null` until explicitly set via Update Staff Profile (there's no profile row created automatically by Create Staff). Not sensitive data; never masked, no extra permission needed beyond `admin_staff.view`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `admin_staff.edit`.

**Validation** — every field optional (captured progressively, not necessarily all at once); send `null` for any field you don't want to set yet.
- `dateOfBirth` — ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), no past/future constraint enforced.
- `gender` — one of `MALE` / `FEMALE` / `OTHER`.
- `addressLine` — max 255 chars.
- `pincode` — max 10 chars (no numeric/format check — deliberately permissive, see KYC's note below for the same rationale).

**Behavior:** full replace of all 4 fields (not a merge) — omitting a field that was previously set clears it to `null`. Creates the profile row on first write if it doesn't exist yet.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target is a super-admin account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

Audits `STAFF_PROFILE_UPDATED`.

**Permission:** `admin_staff.view` (for masked values) — see below for unmasked.

Returns `{aadhaarNumber, panNumber, uanNumber, pfNumber, esicNumber}` — all `null` until set. Values are **encrypted at rest** (AES-256-GCM, random IV per value, via `PiiEncryptor`/`EncryptedStringConverter` — transparent to this API, decrypted on read).

**Masking:** `admin_staff.view` alone (checked at the controller for both GET and PUT) only ever returns **masked** values — all but the last 4 characters replaced with `*` (e.g. `"********9012"`), or fully masked if the value is 4 characters or shorter. Seeing the **unmasked** value additionally requires `admin_staff.view_kyc`, which by default only the **Senior Developer** and **Junior Developer** seed roles hold. Masking is applied purely in the response — the stored value is unaffected either way.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `admin_staff.edit` (the write side has no separate "can write KYC" permission — `admin_staff.edit` alone is sufficient, deliberately, to avoid an unused extra knob; only *reading* unmasked is gated further).

**Validation** — every field optional (progressive capture): `aadhaarNumber`/`panNumber`/`uanNumber` max 20 chars, `pfNumber` max 50, `esicNumber` max 30. **Deliberately no format/checksum validation** (e.g. Aadhaar's 12-digit pattern, PAN's checksum letter) — only a length cap, to avoid rejecting legitimate input against a guessed-at pattern that might not match real-world data exactly.

**Behavior:** full replace of all 5 fields. Creates the KYC row on first write if it doesn't exist yet. The response is masked using the exact same rule as Get Staff KYC — note that even the admin who just *wrote* a value gets it back masked if they only hold `admin_staff.view`, not `admin_staff.edit`+`admin_staff.view_kyc` together.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target is a super-admin account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |
| Any field exceeds its max length | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

Audits `STAFF_KYC_UPDATED`.

**Permission:** `admin_staff.view` (for a masked account number) — see below for unmasked.

Returns `{accountHolderName, bankName, accountNumber, ifscCode, branchName}` — all `null` until set. `accountNumber` is **encrypted at rest** (same mechanism as KYC).

**Masking:** `accountNumber` follows the exact same masking rule as KYC above, gated by `admin_staff.view_bank_details` instead of `admin_staff.view_kyc` (same two seed roles hold it by default, but they're two independent permission codes — holding one does not imply the other). `accountHolderName`, `bankName`, `ifscCode`, `branchName` are **never masked** — only the account number is treated as sensitive here.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `admin_staff.edit` (same reasoning as Update Staff KYC — no separate write permission).

**Validation** — every field optional (progressive capture): `accountHolderName`/`bankName`/`branchName` max 150 chars, `accountNumber` max 30, `ifscCode` max 15. No IFSC-format or account-number-checksum validation, same rationale as KYC.

**Behavior:** full replace of all 5 fields. Creates the row on first write if it doesn't exist yet. The response's `accountNumber` is masked using the same rule as Get Staff Bank Detail.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Staff id doesn't exist | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target is a super-admin account | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |
| Any field exceeds its max length | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

Audits `STAFF_BANK_DETAIL_UPDATED`.

item.name: Health
item.description: Public, unauthenticated (top-level status only — see the request's own description for when component detail appears).

request.description:
**Permission:** none — path is public (`/actuator/health/**` is in `SecurityConfig.PUBLIC_PATHS`).

Returns `{"status": "UP"}` when healthy, with no request body validation or application-specific error codes (this is a Spring Boot Actuator endpoint, not part of the `ApiResponse` envelope used everywhere else in this collection).

**Component detail** (`components: {db: {...}, redis: {...}, ...}`, `mail` excluded via `management.health.mail.enabled=false`) only appears when the request carries a **valid, authenticated** bearer token — `management.endpoint.health.show-details=when-authorized` with no specific role configured, so any authenticated principal (not just one holding a particular permission) sees it; a fully anonymous request only ever sees the bare top-level `status`.
